title: Research Title Examples and How to Write One | AnswerThis
summary: A good research title names the variables, population, setting and design. See 40 research title examples for students and make your own in five steps.
body_markdown:
A good research title tells readers exactly what you studied: the main variables or topic, the population, the setting and, often, the research design. For example, “Study Habits and Academic Performance of Grade 11 STEM Students in a Public Senior High School in Laguna” names two variables, one group of students and one place, in under 20 words.


Below are the three patterns most titles follow, five steps from topic to title, 40 research title examples for students by field, and 10 weak titles rewritten.


## TL;DR


-


Name the variables or phenomenon, the population, the setting and, when it helps, the design.


-


Quantitative titles name variables. Qualitative titles name an experience and the people living it.


-


Build the title from your research question.


-


APA Style sets no maximum length, but asks for focused titles with key terms.


## What makes a good research title?


Your panel, your adviser and anyone searching a database should know what your study is about from the title alone. Four elements do that work:


-


Variables or phenomenon: what you measured, such as burnout, or explored, such as coping strategies.


-


Population: “Grade 11 STEM students,” not just “students.”


-


Setting: a school, barangay, hospital or city.


-


Design: words like “correlational” or “phenomenological,” often added as a subtitle.


## What are the three research title patterns?


The pattern depends on the kind of study. In senior high school, Practical Research 1 usually calls for qualitative research and Practical Research 2 for quantitative research, so you will likely use both.


### Quantitative titles


-


\[Variable 1\] and \[Variable 2\] Among \[Population\] in \[Setting\], for a correlational study


-


Effect of \[Intervention\] on \[Outcome\] of \[Population\]: A Quasi-Experimental Study


-


Level of \[Variable\] Among \[Population\] in \[Setting\], for a descriptive study


Use “effect” only when your design can show cause and effect, as an experiment can. For a survey, use “and” or “relationship between.”


### Qualitative titles


-


Lived Experiences of \[Population\] in \[Situation or Setting\]


-


Challenges (or Coping Strategies) of \[Population\] in \[Setting\]


-


\[Phenomenon\] Among \[Population\]: A Phenomenological Study (or A Case Study)


### Mixed methods titles


These combine measurement and exploration, and usually say so in a subtitle: \[What You Measured\] and \[What You Explored\] Among \[Population\]: A Mixed Methods Study.


## How do you make a research title in 5 steps?


1.


Pick a topic you can actually study. If you are stuck, our[research topic generator](https://answerthis.io/topic-generator) suggests eight ideas from your subject and any limits your teacher has set.


2.


Turn it into a research question. The title answers “what did you study?”, and the question supplies that answer. Our[strong research question examples](https://answerthis.io/blog/research-question-examples) show how to make one specific.


3.


List the key terms: variables or phenomenon, population, setting and design.


4.


Draft three or four titles using a pattern, with the main variables or phenomenon first.


5.


Refine. Cut filler, spell out abbreviations and check the title matches your plan. Then search[Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/) and[Philippine E-Journals](https://ejournals.ph/) for similar titles, and show your adviser.


For example, the question “How do college students who work part-time manage their studies?” becomes “Lived Experiences of Working College Students in a State University in Manila: A Phenomenological Study.”


If you have a short abstract of your planned study, the AnswerThis[research title generator](https://answerthis.io/research-title-generator) can help with step 4. Paste in the abstract and you get 10 suggested titles, and each browser gets three free runs. Because it works from your abstract, the suggestions reflect your own study. Before you settle on one, search Google Scholar or your field’s main database to make sure it is not already in use. Need the abstract first? See[how to write an abstract](https://answerthis.io/blog/how-to-write-an-abstract) .


## 40 research title examples for students


Swap in your own population and setting, but keep a design you can actually carry out.

-

-

-

-

## Weak vs strong research titles


Most fixes add a population and setting, or cut words that carry no information.


Weak title


Stronger title


What changed


Social Media and Students


Time Spent on TikTok and Study Habits of Grade 12 Students in a Private School in Davao City


Names the variables, population and setting


A Study of Bullying


Bystander Behavior Toward Cyberbullying Among Grade 9 Students in a Public High School in Iloilo City


Drops “A Study of,” narrows the topic


The Effects of Online Games on Students


Hours Spent on Online Games and the Academic Performance of Grade 10 Students in Quezon City


Drops “effects,” which a survey cannot show


COVID-19 and Nurses


Coping Strategies of Emergency Room Nurses in a Tertiary Hospital in Manila During the COVID-19 Pandemic


Names the phenomenon, group and setting


Why Do Students Fail Math?


Factors Associated With Low Performance in General Mathematics Among Grade 11 Business Students in General Santos City


Turns a vague question into key terms


An Analysis of the Effectiveness of the Use of Self-Learning Modules


Effectiveness of Self-Learning Modules on the Science Scores of Grade 7 Learners: A Quasi-Experimental Study


Cuts filler, adds population and design


Perceptions of the 4Ps


Perceptions of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program Among Beneficiary Households in a Rural Barangay in Samar


Spells out the acronym, adds the setting


Improving Customer Satisfaction


Service Quality and Customer Satisfaction in Milk Tea Shops in Baguio City


Names what was measured, not a goal


Plastic Pollution: A Big Problem


Single-Use Plastic Consumption Among Households in a Coastal Barangay in Batangas


Replaces an opinion with a variable


Is Remote Work Better?


Work-Life Balance of Remote and On-Site Call Center Agents in Cebu City: A Comparative Study


States what is compared, among whom and where


## How long should a research title be, and how is it formatted?


APA Style sets no word limit. Its[title page guidance](https://apastyle.apa.org/style-grammar-guidelines/paper-format/title-page) says there is no maximum length, but asks you to keep titles focused and include key terms. If yours runs past about 20 words, look for filler.


On an APA 7 student title page, the title is bold, centered, three to four lines from the top, with major words capitalized. Our[APA title page](https://answerthis.io/blog/apa-title-page) guide shows the full layout. Many Philippine schools use their own format, such as all capital letters, so follow your research manual where it differs.


## What are the most common mistakes?


-


Too broad. “Mental Health of Students” could be a book. Say which students, where, and which aspect.


-


Opening with “A Study of” or “An Analysis of.” Every research title describes a study, so these words add nothing. A design subtitle such as “A Phenomenological Study” is different, because it tells readers how you did the work.


-


Unfamiliar abbreviations. Spell out program names and local acronyms. Well-known terms such as STEM and COVID-19 are usually fine.


-


Overclaiming. “Effects of” or “Impact of” in a survey title promises a cause-and-effect finding your data cannot support.


-


Clever instead of clear. If you want a catchy main title, add a subtitle with the variables and population.


## FAQs


### What is the difference between a research topic and a research title?


A topic is the broad area, such as social media use. A title names one specific study within it, with its variables, population and setting.


### Can a research title be a question?


Yes, if it still names the key terms. Many advisers prefer a statement, so check first.


### Should a research title include the research design?


It often helps, especially for qualitative and experimental studies, and many Philippine schools expect it. Add it as a subtitle, such as “A Correlational Study.”


### Should I write the title before or after the research?


Both. Write a working title for your proposal, then revise it once your methods and results are settled, so it describes the study you actually did.


### Can I use the same title as an existing study?


Avoid it. Search Google Scholar, your library and Philippine E-Journals first, and change the population, setting or variables if a very similar study exists. If you are deliberately replicating a study, say so in your paper and cite the original.


Once you have a draft abstract, try the[research title generator](https://answerthis.io/research-title-generator) for 10 more options, then pick the one that best matches your study.
